steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Earth rotates from west to east on its axis, completing one rotation in approximately 23 hours 56 minutes (one sidereal day).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A solar day (24 hours) is the time for the Sun to return to the same position in the sky; a sidereal day (23h 56m 4s) is the time for one complete 360° rotation relative to the stars.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The difference between solar and sidereal days (about 4 minutes) occurs because the Earth orbits the Sun, so the Sun appears to move eastward against the background stars by about 1° per day.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The apparent daily motion of celestial objects (rising in the east, setting in the west) is caused by the Earth's rotation from west to east.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always state that Earth rotates west to east — this explains why objects appear to move east to west. Know the exact values: sidereal day = 23h 56m 4s; solar day = 24h; difference = ~4 minutes. For circumpolar star questions, the rule is: stars within (90° - latitude) of the pole are circumpolar. From 52°N, stars within 38° of the north celestial pole. The Foucault pendulum is the classic evidence for rotation — learn how it works at different latitudes.
